sections.name: OtpService
sections.title: Making, checking and reading codes
sections.what: Makes a random six-digit code and saves it for five minutes under the email or phone. Checking deletes the code on success so it works once. A separate helper returns the live code for development.
sections.why: Likely reason: one-time codes should be short-lived and single-use.
sections.watch_out: The code uses a general random number generator that is not built for security, so codes could be predicted in theory.

summary: Creates six-digit one-time codes, stores them in Redis for five minutes, and checks them once.
purpose: Supports one-time code sign-in and contact verification.
why: Likely reason: Redis expires the codes on its own, so they cannot be used after five minutes.
how: Generating a code picks six random digits and saves them under a prefix plus the email or phone, with a five-minute expiry. Checking compares the stored value and deletes it on a match. A helper reads the stored value for development.
inputs: An identifier (email or phone), and the code to check.
outputs: A new code string, a true or false result for a check, or the stored code for development.
risks: Codes come from a general random number generator that is not built for security. No limit on failed guesses is kept here. The development helper returns the live code.
debug: If codes never work, check the Redis key with the otp prefix and the identifier. Confirm the identifier matches exactly between sending and checking, including any plus sign. Codes older than five minutes are gone.
